arxiv-1811-11071.title: Theoretical design of a strain − - controlled nanoporous CN membrane for helium separation Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-1811-11071.creator: Yong-Chao Rao, Zhao-Qin Chu, Xiao Gu, Xiang-Mei Duan ∗
arxiv-1811-11071.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Yong-Chao Rao, Zhao-Qin Chu, Xiao Gu, Xiang-Mei Duan ∗. Designing an efficient membrane for He purification is quite crucial in scientific and industrial applications. Ultrathin membranes with intrinsic pores are highly desirable for gas purification because of their controllable aperture and homogeneous hole distribution. Based on the first − - principles density function theory and molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that the compressively strained graphitic carbon nitride (CN) can effectively purify He from Ne and Ar.

arxiv-2104-01339.title: Possible Assignment of Excited Light S 1 3 {}^{3}S_{1} Vector Mesons
arxiv-2104-01339.creator: Jie-Cheng Feng, 1 Xian-Wei Kang, 2,3 Qi-Fang Lü, 4,5,6 Feng-Shou Zhang 2,3
arxiv-2104-01339.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jie-Cheng Feng, 1 Xian-Wei Kang, 2,3 Qi-Fang Lü, 4,5,6 Feng-Shou Zhang 2,3. We reanalyze the problems in the assignment of 3 S 1 3 {}^{3}S_{1} and 4 S 1 3 {}^{3}S_{1} light mesons, which have not yet been well established with the q ​ q ¯ q\bar{q} quark model. Regge trajectories and the P 0 3 {}^{3}P_{0} decay model are used respectively to study the mass and width of the observed states and predict the missing ones.

arxiv-2207-07438.title: Dynamic Matching with Better-than-2 Approximation in Polylogarithmic Update Time
arxiv-2207-07438.creator: Sayan Bhattacharya, Peter Kiss, Thatchaphol Saranurak, David Wajc
arxiv-2207-07438.description: Abstract We present dynamic algorithms with polylogarithmic update time for estimating the size of the maximum matching of a graph undergoing edge insertions and deletions with approximation ratio strictly better than 2 2 . Specifically, we obtain a 1 + 1 2 + ϵ ≈ 1.707 + ϵ 1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\epsilon\approx 1.707+\epsilon approximation in bipartite graphs and a 1.973 + ϵ 1.

arxiv-2208-01462.title: Physics-informed Deep Super-resolution for Spatiotemporal Data Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2208-01462.creator: Pu Ren, Chengping Rao, Yang Liu, Zihan Ma, Qi Wang, Jian-Xun Wang, Hao Sun
arxiv-2208-01462.description: Abstract High-fidelity simulation of complex physical systems is exorbitantly expensive and inaccessible across spatiotemporal scales. Recently, there has been an increasing interest in leveraging deep learning to augment scientific data based on the coarse-grained simulations, which is of cheap computational expense and retains satisfactory solution accuracy.

arxiv-2308-04279.title: Perturbation Field in The Presence of Uniform Mean Flow: Doppler Effect for Flows and Acoustics
arxiv-2308-04279.creator: Tapan K. Sengupta, Aditi Sengupta, Bhavna Joshi, Prasannabalaji Sundaram
arxiv-2308-04279.description: Abstract Having developed the perturbation equation for a dissipative quiescent medium for planar propagation using the linearized compressible Navier-Stokes equation without the Stokes’ hypothesis Sengupta, Sengupta, and Joshi 2023 , here the same is extended where a uniform mean flow is present in the ambiance to explore the propagation properties for the Doppler effect.

arxiv-2311-15947.title: GloNets: Globally Connected Neural Networks
arxiv-2311-15947.creator: Antonio Di Cecco, Carlo Metta, Marco Fantozzi, Francesco Morandin, Maurizio Parton
arxiv-2311-15947.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Antonio Di Cecco, Carlo Metta, Marco Fantozzi, Francesco Morandin, Maurizio Parton. Deep learning architectures suffer from depth-related performance degradation, limiting the effective depth of neural networks. Approaches like ResNet are able to mitigate this, but they do not completely eliminate the problem. We introduce Globally Connected Neural Networks (GloNet), a novel architecture overcoming depth-related issues, designed to be superimposed on any model, enhancing its depth without increasing complexity or reducing performance.

arxiv-2312-11760.title: Jet Classification Using High-Level Features from Anatomy of Top Jets
arxiv-2312-11760.creator: Amon Furuichi, Sung Hak Lim, Mihoko M. Nojiri
arxiv-2312-11760.description: Abstract Recent advancements in deep learning models have significantly enhanced jet classification performance by analyzing low-level features (LLFs). However, this approach often leads to less interpretable models, emphasizing the need to understand the decision-making process and to identify the high-level features (HLFs) crucial for explaining jet classification.

arxiv-2407-06909.title: Intercepting Unauthorized Aerial Robots in Controlled Airspace Using Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2407-06909.creator: Francisco Giral, Ignacio Gomez, Soledad Le Clainche
arxiv-2407-06909.description: Abstract The proliferation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in controlled airspace presents significant risks, including potential collisions, disruptions to air traffic, and security threats. Ensuring the safe and efficient operation of airspace, particularly in urban environments and near critical infrastructure, necessitates effective methods to intercept unauthorized or non-cooperative UAVs.

arxiv-2602-16886.title: Atomically Precise Electron Beam Sculpting of Bilayer h-BN: The Role of Crystallographic Orientation and Milling Strategy
arxiv-2602-16886.creator: Ondrej Dyck, Andrew R. Lupini, Ivan Vlassiouk, Matthew Brahlek, Rob Moore, Stephen Jesse Center for Nanophase Materials Sciences, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, TN Correspondence: dyckoe@ornl.gov
arxiv-2602-16886.description: Abstract Achieving atomic precision in top-down manufacturing remains a fundamental challenge nanofabrication technology. Here, the focused electron beam of a scanning transmission electron microscope is used to demonstrate atomically precise sculpting of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) bilayers, achieving nanoribbons as narrow as 6 Å with atomically smooth edges.

This searching behavior is coupled with infection risk due to sniffing both scent marks as well as nasal and anogenital areas of females, which harbor b

pmc-11272186.title: Autophagy in Disease Onset and Progression
pmc-11272186.creator: Hao Wang, Xiushen Li, Qi Zhang, Chengtao Fu, Wenjie Jiang, Jun Xue, Shan Liu, Qingxue Meng, Lisha Ai, Xuejun Zhi, Shoulong Deng, Weizheng Liang
pmc-11272186.description: Autophagy is a biological phenomenon whereby components of cells can self-degrade using autophagosomes. During this process, cells can clear dysfunctional organelles or unwanted elements. Autophagy can recycle unnecessary biomolecules into new components or sometimes, even destroy the cells themselves. This cellular process was first observed in 1962 by Keith R. Porter et al.

pmc-11324740.title: Robust automated calcification meshing for personalized cardiovascular biomechanics
pmc-11324740.creator: Daniel H Pak, Minliang Liu, Theodore Kim, Caglar Ozturk, Raymond McKay, Ellen T Roche, Rudolph Gleason, James S Duncan
pmc-11324740.description: Calcification has significant influence over cardiovascular diseases and interventions. Detailed characterization of calcification is thus desired for predictive modeling, but calcium deposits on cardiovascular structures are still often manually reconstructed for physics-driven simulations. This poses a major bottleneck for large-scale adoption of computational simulations for research or clinical use.

pmc-11359487.title: Osteoblastic Cell Sheet Engineering Using P(VCL-HEMA)-Based Thermosensitive Hydrogels Doped with pVCL@Icariin Nanoparticles Obtained with Supercritical CO2-SAS
pmc-11359487.creator: Rubén García-Sobrino, Isabel Casado-Losada, Carmen Caltagirone, Ana García-Crespo, Carolina García, Juan Rodríguez-Hernández, Helmut Reinecke, Alberto Gallardo, Carlos Elvira, Enrique Martínez-Campos, Barbara Onida, Mauro Banchero, Marta Gallo
pmc-11359487.description: New clinical strategies for treating severe bone and cartilage injuries are required, especially for use in combination with implant procedures. For this purpose, p(VCL-co-HEMA) thermosensitive hydrogels have been activated with icariin-loaded nanoparticles to be used as bone-cell-harvesting platforms. Supercritical CO2-SAS technology has been applied to encapsulate icariin, a small molecule that is involved in osteoblastic differentiation.

pmc-11528038.title: PROTOCOL: The association between adverse childhood experiences and employment outcomes: Protocol for a systematic review
pmc-11528038.creator: Amarech Obse, Evdoxia Gkaintatzi, Paul McCrone
pmc-11528038.description: There is growing evidence of a link between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and health and economic outcomes. Previous systematic reviews synthesised evidence of the relationships between ACEs and various health and some economic outcomes such as healthcare costs and educational attainment.

pmc-12489916.title: Walnut kernel pellicle polyphenols: subcritical water extraction, digestive characteristics, and their effect on gut microbiota and metabolites
pmc-12489916.creator: Xinyu Yuan, Qiqi Feng, Qing Wang, Tao Wang, Zhu Qiao, Hongyu Pan, Yujie Zhong, Yongliang Zhuang
pmc-12489916.description: Walnut kernel pellicle, a by-product of the walnut industry, is rich in polyphenols. However, research on walnut kernel pellicle polyphenols (WPP) remains limited, and the composition and bioactivity of WPP are influenced by extraction methods, gastrointestinal digestion, and colonic fermentation. Therefore, this study aimed to optimize subcritical water extraction (SWE) and NKA-9 resin purification of WPP.

pmc-12607439.title: The Role of Porphyromonas gingivalis in Oral Carcinogenesis and Progression by Remodelling the Tumour Microenvironment: A Narrative Review
pmc-12607439.creator: Katarzyna Starska-Kowarska, Gema Jiménez-González, Carmen Griñán-Lisón, Gianluca Tenore
pmc-12607439.description: Simple SummaryPorphyromonas gingivalis, a Gram-negative anaerobic bacterium is the main inhabitant of the subgingival tissues in the oral cavity. Its presence has been associated with dysbiosis, periodontitis, a pro-inflammatory environment, and oral cancer due its secretion of virulence factors and ability to disrupt signalling pathways related to inter alia epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and cell-cycling.

pmc-12620443.title: Understanding public awareness and knowledge of lung cancer screening practices: a cross-sectional study from the Asir region, Saudi Arabia
pmc-12620443.creator: Geetha Kandasamy, Khalid Orayj, Asma M. Alshahrani, Tahani S. Alanazi, Amjad Hmlan, Sitah Alharthi, Hanan Alyami, Arwa Khaled
pmc-12620443.description: BackgroundLung Cancer (LC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths globally, primarily due to late-stage diagnosis and inadequate public awareness of early symptoms and available screening methods. In Saudi Arabia, rising smoking rates and environmental risks increase the burden, particularly in regions like Asir.

pmc-12643651.title: Three Dimensional-CTA versus Doppler Ultrasound for Anterolateral Thigh Flap Reconstruction in Limb Defects: A Retrospective Study
pmc-12643651.creator: Longhua Yu, Yong Jiang, Jin Zhang, Huagang Zhang, Dazhi Yu, Yanqing Chen, Haiyu Fan, Xiuzhong Li
pmc-12643651.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Soft tissue limb defects often require anterolateral thigh (ALT) flap reconstruction, but anatomical variability of perforator vessels poses a challenge. The comparative efficacy of 3-dimensional computed tomographic angiography (3D-CTA) and color Doppler ultrasonography (CDUS) for preoperative planning remains unclear.Methods:This retrospective study analyzed 95 patients who underwent ALT flap limb reconstruction between March 2017 and May 2023, comparing a 3D-CTA–guided group (n=45) with a CDUS-guided group (n=50).

pmc-12717042.title: Group membership biases children’s evaluation of evidence
pmc-12717042.creator: Joshua A. Confer, Allison M. Champ, Dorsa Amir, Hanna Schleihauf, Jan M. Engelmann
pmc-12717042.description: People form beliefs not only as individual agents, but as members of social groups. Here, we investigate how group membership influences belief formation and revision in childhood. Across three studies (N = 262), 4–6-year-old children either joined one of two groups or neither group, then evaluated evidence to arrive at a conclusion.

pmc-12773534.title: Abstract 223: Pre‐Thrombectomy Diagnosis of Large Vessel Occlusion with Underlying Intracranial Atherosclerotic Disease
pmc-12773534.creator: Mohamed A Tarek, Mateus Damiani, Mahmoud H Mohammaden, Srikant Rangaraju, Pedro N Martins, Jay N Dolia, Aqueel A Pabaney, Jonathan R Grossberg, Michael Nahhas, Alhamza R Nogueira, Raul G Haussen
pmc-12773534.description: IntroductionIntracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) is one of the leading causes of ischemic stroke. We sought to identify variables associated with ICAD underlying large vessel occlusion strokes (LVOS) to facilitate pre‐procedural diagnosis.MethodsRetrospective analysis of a prospectively collected thrombectomy single comprehensive stroke center database. Inclusion criteria: anterior circulation occlusion involving the intracranial ICA, MCA‐M1/M2/M3 or ACA(A1‐A2‐A3).

pmc-13006682.title: Enhancing college students’ AI literacy through generative AI use: a mixed-methods investigation
pmc-13006682.creator: Jingsheng Wang, Bing Bai, Qi An
pmc-13006682.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education has created a paradoxical landscape for college students: while technological advancements offer unprecedented convenience, they simultaneously exacerbate the knowledge-practice gap in AI Literacy cultivation. Traditional educational frameworks struggle to address the dynamic interplay between AI-mediated learning environments, ethical dilemmas, and competency development, leaving a critical theoretical and practical void in literacy cultivation models.

pmc-13078162.title: Follicular lymphoma within an ovarian teratoma
pmc-13078162.creator: Franceska Tchapdeu, Neha Bhardwaj, Jay Dhanapal, John Willan
pmc-13078162.description: We report an unusual case of a 46 year old diagnosed with follicular lymphoma within an ovarian teratoma. She sought medical attention due to menorrhagia, but was otherwise well. Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scanning demonstrated stage III disease, and she was treated with combination chemotherapy to complete metabolic remission on her end of treatment PET scan.

pmc-13095505.title: BAR12: Bayesian Autoregressive Phase 1‐2 Design for Cell Therapy Trials With Manufacturing Changes
pmc-13095505.creator: Cheng‐Han Yang, Peter F. Thall, David Marin, Sheferaw Y. Belay, Ruitao Lin
pmc-13095505.description: An early phase dose‐finding trial of a new cell therapy may involve one or more manufacturing modifications made during the trial, known as “tweaks,” to improve the cell product quality. For example, a tweak may change the cell culture duration, cytokine cocktail, or donor criteria.

pmc-13240545.title: Long QT Syndrome Type 5 With Coexisting KCNE1 and RYR2 Variants: A Diagnostic Ambiguity
pmc-13240545.creator: Mohammad Hossein Nikoo, Hossein Fatemian, Amir Hossein Hassani, Mehrdad Rabiee Rad, Sara Mostafavi
pmc-13240545.description: Long QT syndrome (LQTS) predisposes to syncope and sudden cardiac death. Type 5 LQTS, linked to KCNE1 variants, is rare. A teenage female presented with recurrent syncope. ECG showed QTc 485 ms. Genetic testing identified KCNE1 and RYR2 variants. Beta‐blockers and ICD prevented events. The case highlights diagnostic and genotype–phenotype challenges.

pmc-13477758.title: Reliability and Validity of Isometric Back Extensor Strength Measurements Using Hand-Held and Isokinetic Dynamometry in Sitting and Semi-Standing Positions
pmc-13477758.creator: Tomohiro Nakatani, Masakazu Minetama, Yoshio Yamamoto, Yukihiro Nakagawa
pmc-13477758.description: Introduction The prone position is generally regarded as the standard posture for back extensor strength testing. However, some older adults may have difficulty assuming this position, making alternative approaches more clinically feasible. It remains unclear whether measurements obtained in the sitting and semi-standing positions demonstrate sufficient validity compared with those in the prone position.

pmc-13521934.title: Comparative mitogenomic study of the brown accentor (Prunella fulvescens) and a sympatric relative across an altitudinal gradient
pmc-13521934.creator: Wenshu Zhang, Shaobin Li
pmc-13521934.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The Brown Accentor (Prunella fulvescens) is an understudied bird on the Tibetan Plateau, for which life-history and molecular genetic data remain scarce. In this study, we sequenced the complete mitochondrial genome of P. fulvescens and conducted a comparative analysis with two conspecific individuals (one from the similar altitude and one from a lower altitude); we further performed interspecific comparison with its sympatric species Prunella strophiata (a congener) and Carpodacus rubicilloides (a sympatric non-congener). Divergence between high and lower altitude populations of P.

pmc-13642099.title: Self‐Interfering Magnetic Dipole Transition Emission in Rare‐Earth Ions Doped Nanoparticles Modulated by Plasmonic Mirror Nanocavity
pmc-13642099.creator: Chengxiang Gou, Bowen Kang, Wangze Li, Xiangtai Xi, Yuting Luo, Jiaqi Wang, Zhengkun Fu, Huan Chen, Zhenglong Zhang, Hairong Zheng
pmc-13642099.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In conventional photonics, light–matter interactions are predominantly governed by electric dipole (ED) transition. Although magnetic dipole (MD) transition emission is challenging to detect due to its intrinsic properties, it exhibited significant application potential in biological probes and quantum technologies. Eu3+ ions are considered an ideal system for investigating MD–ED transition emissions owing to their unique energy‐level structure as sensitive nanoscale probes for electromagnetic fields.
